summary: A 1957 L-4 lookout house on a 53-ft tower north of Missoula, vacant since its 2005-2012 restoration and now a stop for hikers and backpackers.

facts.design: 1936-pattern L-4 lookout house on a 53-ft timber tower

access.note: Hikers and backpackers visit the site and some stay in the house. No closure was found in the sources read. The nomination says difficult access and the tower's perceived danger kept it out of the rental program.

visit.trail_note: The site was first reached only by pack trail; a 13-mile road from Gold Creek was built later. Current road condition was not confirmed.

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Lolo National Forest (Missoula Ranger District)

events.note: Earlier pole tower with an L-4 cab, dated 1935 by firelookout.com and by the nomination citing Kresek. The NHLR gives 1936 for the kit.
Lolo National Forest built the current 1936-pattern L-4 house, replacing the earlier lookout.
Manned as a primary lookout point from 1957 to 1967.
One of twenty-six lookouts the Lolo forest planned to man for the 1967 fire season.
Inspection found few first-discovery fires (average 1.4 for 1958-1967); site downgraded to an emergency lookout.
Manned only during extreme fire danger; began to deteriorate.
Sat vacant with little or no maintenance until about 2005.
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register, March 1, 1997.
Missoula Ranger District began restoration after an inspection found the tower in stable condition.
Windows removed in 2006 for restoration at the Region 1 Historic Preservation Team shop; reinstalled July and August 2008.
Regional preservation team and volunteers installed a new sawn cedar shingle roof.
Listed on the National Register of Historic Places (NRIS 100002042), date listed January 29, 2018.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The record's 2233 m matches the NHLR's 7,326 ft. The nomination gives 7,447 ft, Historic Montana says nearly 7,500 ft, and firelookout.com gives 6,704 ft. The story reports the spread and keeps the NHLR figure.
firelookout.com says Flathead County. The NHLR and the nomination both say Missoula County, which is what the record uses. The firelookout.com county is an error.

firelookout.com and the nomination (citing Kresek) date the earlier pole-tower L-4 to 1935. The NHLR says the forest topped the tower with a kit in 1936. The 1957 date for the current house agrees across sources.

notes_for_editor: History from 1957 to 2018 is well sourced by the NRHP nomination. Present-day status and access rest on the nomination (form dated November 2, 2017), not a 2026 check; confirm with the Missoula Ranger District before publishing. Access level public is an inference from hikers visiting, not a posted status. height_m 16.2 is converted from 53 ft. firelookout.com's county and elevation are wrong or disputed. No photos added. Fact-check 2026-10-08: story reworded where it copied source wording, 'now serves' changed to the 2017 nomination's date, and evidence added for the 2006 shop move, the kit, the Missoula County claim and the vacancy.
